title: Append Mode

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: In this lesson you will learn how append mode adds new text to the end without erasing what was already there.
learn: Write more lines at the end
idea: Mode "a" means append. New text is added at the end. Old text stays. f = open("log.txt", "a") then f.write("new line\n"). Use "w" to replace; use "a" to add.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, append a third day: change the append write to include an extra line, or add another write before close. Press Run and check three days appear.

practice.text: Create memo.txt with "Hello\n" using "w", then append "Again\n", then print the file.
practice.hint: After the first close(), open memo.txt again with mode "a" (append), write "Again\n", close, then read and print like the starter shows.
practice.starterTip: Add: f = open("memo.txt", "a"), then f.write("Again\n"), then f.close() in the "# Append Again" section.
practice.starter:
f = open("memo.txt", "w")
f.write("Hello\n")
f.close()
# Append Again

f = open("memo.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if memo has Hello and Again using append, then printed.

practice.text: Append one new tip line to tips.txt, then print the whole tips file.
practice.hint: You already opened tips.txt in append mode. f.write() adds at the end. Include \n so your tip is on its own line.
practice.starterTip: Try f.write("Take breaks when coding.\n") or any short tip you like, then run and check all tips print.
practice.starter:
f = open("tips.txt", "a")
f.write()
f.close()
f = open("tips.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if tips.txt grows by one line via append and is printed.

quiz.question: What does mode "a" do?

options.text: Erases the whole file first always

quiz.correct: Append keeps old text and adds more.

quiz.question: How is "a" different from "w"?
quiz.correct: Choose w to replace, a to add.
quiz.wrong: Write vs append is the key idea.

quiz.question: After appending, does the first line still exist?
quiz.wrong: Old lines stay when you append.

project.title: Practice Log
project.desc: Write a first log line with w, append two more days with a, then print the full log.
project.starter:
f = open("practice_log.txt", "w")
f.write("Day 1\n")
f.close()
# Append Day 2 and Day 3
